Until now you wrote SQL by hand and ran it yourself in DuckDB. In real teams nobody works like that for long: there are hundreds of queries, they depend on each other, and they must run every night in the right order, in a development copy and in production. dbt is the tool that organises this work. In this chapter you install nothing new (
already installed dbt) but you create your first
, connect it to your practice database, run it, and look inside every folder it creates.
For the exam, this chapter is the base of everything. Many questions show a piece of

, and ask what happens. If you know exactly what each file is for and what dbt does when you press
, those questions become easy points. You also meet the dbt platform (the web version of dbt), because the exam talks about both.
A dbt project is a folder with a
file; dbt reads it, finds your models, and uses a separate file,

, to know how to connect to the warehouse. Every command first parses the project into a manifest (the map of all your models and their links), then compiles the Jinja into plain SQL, and only then sends that SQL to the warehouse. Everything dbt produces lands in
, which you never commit to Git, while the project files themselves live in a Git repository from the first day.
